title: Lecture 1: The Geometry of Linear Equations

segments.text: The roadmap is to solve linear equations through three views: a row picture, a column picture, and the compact matrix form Ax equals b.
Start with a concrete example of two equations and two unknowns. Write the coefficient matrix, the unknown vector, and the right-hand-side vector.
Draw each equation as a line. Ask where the two lines meet, then check that the intersection satisfies both equations.
Now switch to the column picture. Combine scaled column vectors to reach b; this picture gives intuition for the formal idea of a linear combination.
Compare the row and column views. The same solution is an intersection in one picture and the required combination in the other.
Move from the simple two-dimensional example to three equations and then ask what changes in higher dimensions. Generalize the picture even when it cannot be drawn.
